title: Facebook and Instagram ran nudify-app ads from a single Chinese firm, watchdog says
excerpt: Awatchdog group says Meta ran thousands of advertisements for apps that digitally undress women, and that the network placing them traces back to a single company in China. The finding lands on a platform that has spent more than a year insisting it is winning this fight, even as it fields separate lawsuits over scam ads elsewhere […]
content_html:
Awatchdog group says Meta ran thousands of advertisements for apps that digitally undress women, and that the network placing them traces back to a single company in China. The finding lands on a platform that has spent more than a year insisting it is winning this fight, even as it fields separate lawsuits over scam ads elsewhere on its services.

The Tech Transparency Project published its findings  identifying 210 Facebook pages tied to a Chinese firm it calls GatherOne. Together those pages ran roughly 30,800 ads for face-swapping and AI tools, and 43 of them ran more than 7,600 ads for apps built to produce non-consensual imagery of women, according to the report.

GatherOne, which the group links to entities registered in Beijing and Hong Kong and to a controlling shareholder named Wang Hao, sits at the centre of the operation. After the report appeared, the company said it would suspend new ad applications for its AI nudify services.

Meta’s own enforcement record tells the rest of the story. Of the 210 pages, 179, or 85%, ran ads the company itself later removed for breaching its standards on adult sexual exploitation, sexual solicitation, and nudity, many of them showing women simulating sex acts.

Meta removed ads and disabled accounts during the investigation, but the group found parts of the network still live. A spokesperson said the company takes “aggressive steps” against such apps, and did not answer the group’s specific questions.

In early 2025 it shared more than 3,800 URLs for nudify apps with other technology firms through an industry programme called Lantern, and it says it has since built detection tools aimed at this category of ad. The report suggests those tools are not keeping pace with the advertisers gaming them.

None of this is new. In June 2025 Meta sued Joy Timeline HK Limited, the Hong Kong maker of an app called CrushAI, after it ran more than 87,000 ads across at least 135 Facebook pages. The company said it had been acting against the advertiser since 2023, echoing an Indian order last year to pull child abuse ads from Instagram.

Those ads were not subtle. Many promised users the ability to “erase any clothes” from a photograph, and the tools were marketed mainly at people in the US, Canada, the UK, Australia, and Germany. CBS News had surfaced hundreds of them months before Meta filed suit.

The lawsuit did not stop the ads. Researchers at the American Sunlight Project and Indicator counted 4,215 more nudify ads in the three months after Meta announced new detection technology, ads that reached an estimated 359,547 users in the EU and UK alone. Even when the company blocked the ads for a flagged website, the operators had often already run hundreds more through fresh pages and accounts.

Some advertisers had registered under names such as “ddd” and “111”, which researchers said breaches the transparency rules in the EU’s Digital Services Act, the law that requires platforms to disclose who is paying for each ad. That gap matters, because a network hidden behind nonsense names is one regulators cannot easily follow to a bank account.

The reports arrive as regulators close in. The TAKE IT DOWN Act, signed into US law in May 2025, requires platforms to remove non-consensual intimate imagery within 48 hours of a valid request and gives the Federal Trade Commission the power to enforce it, with the main compliance deadline falling this year.

UK, meanwhile, is moving to criminalise the creation of sexually explicit deepfakes, part of a wider reckoning that turned the Taylor Swift deepfake deluge into a wake-up call for lawmakers. The through line in all of it is the same: the ads keep running because automated review keeps waving them through, and the money keeps arriving from somewhere Meta says it cannot fully see.

content_html_zh:
Awatchdog 组织表示，Meta 投放了数千个以数字方式脱掉女性衣服的应用程序广告，而放置这些广告的网络可以追溯到中国的一家公司。 这一发现落在了一个平台上，该平台花了一年多的时间坚称自己正在赢得这场战斗，尽管该平台就其服务中其他地方的诈骗广告提起了单独的诉讼。

技术透明度项目公布了其调查结果，确定了 210 个 Facebook 页面与一家名为 GatherOne 的中国公司有关。 报告称，这些页面总共发布了大约 30,800 个关于换脸和人工智能工具的广告，其中 43 个页面发布了超过 7,600 个用于生成未经同意的女性图像的应用程序的广告。

GatherOne 处于运营中心，该集团与在北京和香港注册的实体以及名为王浩的控股股东有联系。 该报告发布后，该公司表示将暂停其人工智能裸体服务的新广告应用。

Meta 自己的执法记录说明了故事的其余部分。 在这 210 个页面中，有 179 个（即 85%）刊登了公司后来因违反成人性剥削、性诱惑和裸体标准而删除的广告，其中许多广告展示了模拟性行为的女性。

Meta 在调查期间删除了广告并禁用了帐户，但该小组发现部分网络仍然存在。 一位发言人表示，该公司对此类应用程序采取了“积极措施”，但没有回答该组织的具体问题。

2025 年初，该公司通过名为 Lantern 的行业计划与其他科技公司共享了 3,800 多个裸体应用程序的 URL，并表示此后已针对此类广告构建了检测工具。 该报告表明，这些工具并没有跟上广告商利用它们的步伐。

这些都不是什么新鲜事。 2025 年 6 月，Meta 起诉 Joy Timeline HK Limited（一家名为 CrushAI 的应用程序的香港制造商），因为该公司在至少 135 个 Facebook 页面上投放了超过 87,000 个广告。 该公司表示，自 2023 年以来一直在针对该广告商采取行动，呼应了印度去年下令从 Instagram 上撤下虐待儿童广告的命令。

这些广告并不微妙。 许多人向用户承诺能够从照片中“擦除任何衣服”，这些工具主要面向美国、加拿大、英国、澳大利亚和德国的用户。 在 Meta 提起诉讼的几个月前，哥伦比亚广播公司新闻 (CBS News) 就已经曝光了数百起此类事件。

诉讼并没有停止广告。 在 Meta 宣布新的检测技术后的三个月内，美国阳光项目和指标的研究人员统计了 4,215 个裸体广告，仅在欧盟和英国，这些广告就吸引了 359,547 名用户。 即使该公司屏蔽了被标记网站的广告，运营商通常也已经通过新页面和帐户投放了数百个广告。

一些广告商以“ddd”和“111”等名称进行注册，研究人员表示，这违反了欧盟《数字服务法》中的透明度规则，该法要求平台披露谁为每个广告付费。 这一差距很重要，因为监管机构无法轻易追踪到隐藏在无意义名称背后的网络，从而追踪到银行账户。

这些报告是在监管机构逼近之际发布的。 《TAKE IT DOWN Act》于 2025 年 5 月签署成为美国法律，要求平台在收到有效请求后 48 小时内删除未经同意的亲密图像，并赋予联邦贸易委员会强制执行的权力，主要合规截止日期为今年。

与此同时，英国正着手将制作露骨的深度伪造品定为刑事犯罪，这是更广泛的清算的一部分，该清算将泰勒·斯威夫特的深度伪造品泛滥变成了对立法者的警钟。 所有这一切的主线都是一样的：广告继续投放，因为自动审核不断地让它们通过，而资金不断从 Meta 说它无法完全看到的地方到达。
